hook.text: With 500 notes in his system, he couldn't find anything. He needed a map, not more notes.

buildup.text: A map of content is an index note that curates links to all notes on a theme. It's a table of contents you build.

discovery.text: Maps give you entry points into your note network. Instead of searching blindly, you start from a curated overview.

twist.text: Maps should emerge naturally. Don't create them prematurely. Wait until a cluster of 10-15 notes forms, then map them.

climax.text: Create maps of content for your major interests. Update them as new notes join the cluster.

punchline.text: Too many notes? Build a map. Overview restores clarity.

quiz.question: When should you create a map of content?
options: Before taking any notes on a new topic
When a cluster of 10-15 related notes naturally forms
Only at the end of a semester or project
